CONCLUSION \\nThis study proposes an Out-of-Order (OoO) architecture \\nfor Cyber-Physical Manufacturing Systems (CPMS), \\nleveraging real-time data analytics to enhance the resilience \\nof planning and scheduling under uncertainty. By drawing \\ninspiration from OoO execution in CPU systems, we \\nconstruct a multi-level instruction queuing mechanism that \\nenables dynamic scheduling based on task executability. \\nThe contributions of this work are twofold. First, it \\nintroduces a novel decision-making framework for CPMS \\nthat bridges the structural disconnect between planning and \\nreal-time execution, enabling decentralized and execution-\\naware control. Second, the proposed approach provides a \\nreal-time alternative to traditional data-driven scheduling \\nmethods. Unlike conventional models that rely heavily on \\nhistorical data or pre-trained policies and often address only \\nlimited types of uncertainty, OoO mechanism dynamically \\nadapts to multiple disturbances without offline learning or \\nstatic assumptions.
